reproduction_target: Genome-resource paper for the annelid Capitella teleta. Computational target: de novo chromosome-level assembly of newly generated ONT + Illumina + Hi-C data (basecalling, filtering, Canu assembly, HyPo polishing, Purge Haplotigs, BlobTools decontamination, BUSCO/QUAST QC, BWA-MEM + Arima Hi-C mapping, YaHS scaffolding), repeat/TE annotation (RepeatModeler, RepeatMasker, Kimura landscape), protein-coding gene prediction and functional annotation (STAR, Portcullis, Mikado, Miniprot, Augustus, PASA, BUSCO proteome, Trinotate, PANTHER, AGAT), comparative genomics (OrthoFinder + MMseqs2 + IQ-TREE orthogroups, ETE3 gene family gain/loss, hypergeometric expansion test, topGO enrichment, MetaEuk + rbhXpress + macrosyntR macrosynteny), mitochondrial genome assembly/annotation (BLASTN, MITOS 2 web server, ORFfinder, CGView) and cox1 phylogeny (Clustal Omega, TrimAl, IQ-TREE2, FigTree), bulk RNA-seq re-analysis (SVA, limma, DESeq2, Mfuzz), ATAC-seq re-analysis (cutadapt, NextGenMap, SAMtools, deepTools, MACS3, BEDTools, IDR, DiffBind, Mfuzz, HOMER), EM-seq re-analysis (Trim Galore!, Bismark, custom R scripts), and scRNA-seq re-analysis of PRJNA669754 (Cell Ranger, STAR, Seurat, R). Worm culture, gDNA extraction, ONT/Illumina/Hi-C library prep and sequencing, PCR + Sanger validation of mitochondrial gene order, riboprobe synthesis, whole-mount in situ hybridisation and microscopy are wet-lab (W, out of scope for computational reproduction).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis list built from the bioRxiv v1 JATS XML full text. WebFetch on the .source.xml returned HTTP 403; the XML was retrieved via curl with a browser user-agent (200 OK) and tag-stripped locally. The paper has a short 'Data availability' section (one ENA/DDBJ/GenBank project accession plus a portal reference) and NO code availability statement of any kind. The single GitHub URL in the entire manuscript (https://github.com/ArimaGenomics/mapping_pipeline) is a third-party protocol reference for Hi-C read mapping, not the authors' analysis code, and is cited without tag, release or commit. Custom code is referenced three times in prose without any location: a 'custom-modified version of createRepeatLandscape.pl', 'a Python script' for assembly comparison, and 'custom R scripts' for methylation analysis. Wet-lab steps counted in W, not verdicted.

steps.label: Nanopore basecalling with Guppy (URL cited, NO version) in super-accurate (SUP) mode; r9.4.1 and r10.4.1 pores
Long-read filtering with NanoFilt (v.2.8.0) to retain reads > 3.8 kb
De novo long-read assembly with Canu (v2.2) using 'batOptions= -dg 3 -db 3 -dr 1 -ca 500 -cp 50'
Assembly polishing with HyPo (v.1.0.3) using long reads > 1 kb plus short Illumina reads
Haplotig purging with Purge Haplotigs (v.1.1.2), parameters -l 65 -m 145 -h 300
Decontamination following the BlobTools (v1.1) pipeline, removing contigs with non-animal taxonomy - taxonomy database and its release are not named
Assembly QC with BUSCO (v.5.4.4) and QUAST (v.4.6.1) - no BUSCO lineage dataset (odb version) and no QUAST options stated

Hi-C read mapping with BWA-MEM (v.0.7.17) as single reads, then 'filter_five_end.pl' and 'two_read_bam_combiner.pl' from the Arima Genomics mapping pipeline (https://github.com/ArimaGenomics/mapping_pipeline, no tag/commit pin)
Chromosome-scale scaffolding with YaHS (v.1.2a) - no parameters, no restriction-enzyme setting, no manual-curation record stated
De novo repeat library construction with RepeatModeler (v.2.0.5) plus RepBase (no RepBase release stated), followed by undocumented manual removal of 'potentially bona fide genes' from the library
Repeat/TE annotation and soft-masking with RepeatMasker (v.4.1.5) - no search engine, no options, and the curated library from C10 is not deposited

Kimura substitution level / repeat landscape via 'calcDivergenceFromAlign.pl' and a CUSTOM-MODIFIED version of 'createRepeatLandscape.pl' from RepeatMasker v4.1.0 - the modified script is not provided anywhere
RNA-seq alignment to the soft-masked genome with STAR (v.2.7.11b) using 'all available RNA-seq datasets' - the datasets are not enumerated with accessions and no STAR parameters are given
Splice-junction detection with Portcullis (v.1.2.4) producing a 'curated set' - curation criteria and parameters not stated
Transcript-evidence consolidation with the Mikado (v.2.3.4) pipeline - no configuration file, scoring file or transcript assemblers listed
Spliced alignment of the Owenia fusiformis proteome onto the C. teleta genome with Miniprot (v0.8-r220) - proteome source/version not accessioned, no parameters
Augustus (v.3.5.0) species training on Mikado models and ab initio prediction using exon/intron/gene hints derived from RNA-seq, Portcullis junctions and Miniprot alignments
Final gene set construction with the PASA (v.2.5.2) pipeline combining RNA-seq and ab initio models - no configuration or alignment-assembler settings stated

Gene-model filtering: removal of in-frame stop codons, repeat-overlapping predictions and models with 'high similarity' to TEs in RepeatPeps.lib - no script, no similarity threshold, no overlap fraction
Annotation completeness with BUSCO (v.5.4.4) in proteome mode (95.7% complete reported) - lineage dataset not stated
Functional annotation with the Trinotate pipeline (v.4.0.0) and PANTHER (v.2.2) - no database releases (Swiss-Prot, Pfam, eggNOG) and no e-value cutoffs stated
Old-vs-new assembly/annotation comparison: gff files 'mined in a Python script' (script not provided) with AGAT (NO version) used to extract intronic regions

Orthogroup (gene family) inference with OrthoFinder (v.2.5.5) using MMseqs2 (NO version) and IQ-TREE (NO version) on non-redundant longest-isoform proteomes - the species set and proteome sources are not listed with accessions/versions

Gene family gain/loss and node-of-origin inference by mapping orthogroups onto a reference species phylogeny with the ETE3 library (NO version) via unpublished parsing code; the reference species tree is not deposited

Gene family expansion test: hypergeometric test against the median gene number per species within a family, 'as previously published' - no code, no significance threshold, no multiple-testing correction stated
GO enrichment of lost orthogroups and expanded gene families with topGO (v.2.60.1) and Fisher's exact test - algorithm (classic/weight01) and cutoff not stated

Macrosynteny: MetaEuk (v.6-a5d39d9) annotation of four chromosome-level assemblies, rbhXpress (v.1.2.3) reciprocal-best-BLAST-hit detection, plotting with macrosyntR (v.0.2.19) - source assemblies not accessioned in this paper

Ancestral linkage group assignment from inter-species chromosomal correspondences using published P. maximus / U. unicinctus / L. longissimus annotations - manual/interpretive, no code and no assignment table format specified

Mitochondrial genome recovery by BLASTN (NO version) of Notomastus sp. mitogenome (NCBI LC661358.1) against a de novo assembled transcriptome from a prior study; then MITOS 2 web server (NO version) with default settings and invertebrate genetic code 5, followed by manual protein-coding gene editing using NCBI ORFfinder
Mitochondrial circle plot (gene order, GC content, GC skew) with the online CGView tool (NO version), SVG then edited manually in Adobe Illustrator

cox1 dataset assembly (NCBI BLAST search filtered to genus Capitella, 291 sequences - no accession list deposited), alignment with the online Clustal Omega server (NO version), trimming with TrimAl (v1.5.0, no trimming mode/gap threshold stated)
Maximum-likelihood cox1 phylogeny with IQ-TREE2 (v2.3.6), ultrafast bootstrap 5000 replicates; tree viewed/rooted in FigTree v1.4.4 - substitution model / ModelFinder setting not stated
Bulk RNA-seq batch correction with SVA (v.3.46.0) surrogate variable analysis (null model / full model variables not enumerated)

Batch-effect removal and expression normalisation with Limma (v.3.54.2) and DESeq2 (v.1.38.3) - design formulas and normalisation choices not stated; the underlying bulk RNA-seq accessions are not given in this paper's data availability statement
Soft k-means clustering of expression dynamics with Mfuzz (v.2.58.0), 10 clusters chosen by the elbow method on minimum centroid distance; 346 of 34,679 transcripts with no expression discarded
ATAC-seq adaptor removal and trimming of paired 150-base reads to 75 bases with cutadapt (v.2.5) - adaptor sequences not given
ATAC-seq mapping with NextGenMap (v.0.5.5) in paired-end mode, duplicate removal with SAMtools (v.1.9), read shifting with deepTools (v.3.4.3) - shift offsets not stated
Peak calling with MACS3 (v.3.0.3), settings '-f BAMPE --min-length 100 --max-gap 75' and '-q 0.01'
Filtering of peaks in repetitive regions with BEDTools (v.2.31.1) - subcommand and overlap fraction not stated; the repeat BED derives from the undeposited RepeatMasker output
Reproducible peak identification with IDR (NO version), flag --soft-idr-threshold 0.05

Consensus peak set generation, normalisation and pairwise stage contrasts with DiffBind (v.3.14.0); PCA on variance-stabilising-transformed DiffBind-normalised matrices - normalisation method and contrast thresholds not stated
Peak clustering by accessibility dynamics with Mfuzz (v.2.64.0) - number of clusters and fuzzifier not stated (contrast with C35, where they are)
Peak annotation with HOMER (v.5.1) and per-peak two-sided Pearson correlation between chromatin accessibility and gene expression
EM-seq adaptor/quality trimming with Trim Galore! (v0.6.7), parameters -j 8 -e 0.1 -q 20 -O 1

EM-seq alignment with Bismark (v0.24.0), options '--q --local --score-min G,20,8 --ignore-quals --no-mixed --no-discordant --dovetail --maxins 500', then bismark_methylation_extractor for all cytosine contexts
Downstream methylation analyses from Bismark coverage files with CUSTOM R SCRIPTS cited only to a prior publication - scripts not provided, no versions, no thresholds

scRNA-seq alignment and digital gene expression matrix generation with 10x Genomics Cell Ranger version 8.0.0 using STAR version 2.7.2a, 'standard parameters', run separately against the old and new C. teleta genomes; input reads from SRA BioProject PRJNA669754

Single-cell processing with Seurat version 5.1.0 under R version 4.4.1: QC filters (<=300 / >=1500 genes and UMIs), NormalizeData scale.factor=10000, FindVariableFeatures vst nfeatures=2000, RunPCA, JackStraw dims=100, RunUMAP n.neighbors=25 on 14 PCs, FindClusters algorithm=4 resolution=c(0.5,0.75,1,2,3) n.start=50 random.seed=17, FindMarkers roc/wilcox min.pct=0.25 logfc.threshold=0.25

Manual cluster-resolution selection and subcluster merging: resolutions 'assessed manually', a resolution chosen because it 'seemed most biologically relevant', subclusters with fewer than two differentially expressed genes merged - irreducibly manual, no record of the chosen resolution or the merge map

headline.static_readiness: 0/49 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 23/49 computational steps (C2 NanoFilt 2.8.0, C3 Canu 2.2, C4 HyPo 1.0.3, C5 Purge Haplotigs 1.1.2, C6 BlobTools 1.1, C8 BWA-MEM 0.7.17 + Arima scripts, C17 Augustus 3.5.0, C26 topGO 2.60.1, C27 MetaEuk/rbhXpress/macrosyntR, C32 IQ-TREE2 2.3.6, C33 SVA 3.46.0, C34 limma 3.54.2 + DESeq2 1.38.3, C35 Mfuzz 2.58.0, C36 cutadapt 2.5, C37 NextGenMap 0.5.5 + SAMtools 1.9 + deepTools 3.4.3, C38 MACS3 3.0.3, C39 BEDTools 2.31.1, C41 DiffBind 3.14.0, C43 HOMER 5.1, C44 Trim Galore! 0.6.7, C45 Bismark 0.24.0, C47 Cell Ranger 8.0.0 + STAR 2.7.2a, C48 Seurat 5.1.0 / R 4.4.1). Every one of those reaches RI only because the tool version is exactly pinned in prose AND at least one operational parameter is stated; none can exceed RI because there is no code, no lockfile and no container anywhere. 26/49 steps cap at NI, in three families: (a) version pinned but ZERO parameters stated (C7 BUSCO/QUAST lineage, C9 YaHS, C10 RepeatModeler, C11 RepeatMasker, C13 STAR, C14 Portcullis, C15 Mikado, C16 Miniprot, C18 PASA, C20 BUSCO proteome, C21 Trinotate/PANTHER, C42 Mfuzz peaks); (b) tool carries NO version (C1 Guppy, C23 MMseqs2/IQ-TREE inside OrthoFinder, C29 BLASTN + MITOS 2 web server, C30 CGView online, C31 Clustal Omega online, C40 IDR); (c) the step depends on unpublished CUSTOM CODE or irreducible manual curation (C12 custom-modified createRepeatLandscape.pl, C19 gene-model filtering, C22 'a Python script' + unversioned AGAT, C24 ETE3 gain/loss parsing, C25 hypergeometric expansion test, C28 ancestral linkage group assignment, C46 custom R methylation scripts, C49 manual scRNA cluster curation). There is NO code availability statement; the only GitHub URL in the manuscript is the third-party Arima Hi-C mapping pipeline. No lockfile, container digest or conda spec is claimed, so no step could exceed RI even under stage 2.
headline.coverage: 49 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS XML Methods prose (genome assembly and QC, Hi-C scaffolding, repeat annotation, gene prediction and functional annotation, comparative genomics and macrosynteny, mitochondrial genome and cox1 phylogeny, bulk RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, EM-seq, and scRNA-seq re-analysis). 8 wet-lab step groups counted in W but out of computational-reproduction scope: worm colony maintenance and larval collection/fixation; HMW gDNA extraction (MagAttract); Nanopore r9.4.1/r10.4.1 and Illumina short-read sequencing; Proximo Hi-C (Phase Genomics) library prep and sequencing; PCR amplification, Monarch cleanup and Sanger sequencing for mitochondrial gene-order validation; riboprobe synthesis and Sanger validation; colourimetric whole-mount in situ hybridisation; microscopy imaging (Leica DMRA2 / Infinity5, Helicon Focus, Photoshop/Illustrator).

gaps.where: Whole analysis pipeline (no Code Availability section exists in the paper)
gaps.missing: No analysis code, workflow or script is provided for any of the 49 computational steps. Full-text search of the JATS XML for 'code availability', 'github', 'gitlab', 'zenodo', 'figshare' returns exactly one repository URL, https://github.com/ArimaGenomics/mapping_pipeline, which is a third-party Hi-C mapping protocol cited without tag or commit, not the authors' code. Three custom artefacts are named in prose with no location at all: a 'custom-modified version of createRepeatLandscape.pl' (C12), 'a Python script' for gff mining in assembly comparison (C22), and 'custom R scripts' for downstream methylation analysis (C46).
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the assembly, annotation, comparative-genomics, ATAC/EM-seq/scRNA-seq analysis scripts in a public repository with a tagged release or Zenodo DOI, include the three custom artefacts named above, and add a Code Availability statement to the manuscript.

gaps.where: Whole software environment (assembly stack, annotation stack, R/Bioconductor stack)
gaps.missing: No environment lockfile, container image or digest, conda environment file, renv.lock or module list is claimed anywhere. The Acknowledgements note that the work 'utilised computational resources from the High-Performance Computing Facility Apocrita at Queen Mary University of London', but no module versions or environment export accompany that.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock/pixi lockfile or a container digest pinning the full stack (Guppy, NanoFilt, Canu, HyPo, Purge Haplotigs, BlobTools, BUSCO, QUAST, BWA, YaHS, RepeatModeler/Masker, STAR, Portcullis, Mikado, Miniprot, Augustus, PASA, Trinotate, AGAT, OrthoFinder, MMseqs2, IQ-TREE, MetaEuk, macrosyntR, cutadapt, NextGenMap, SAMtools, deepTools, MACS3, BEDTools, IDR, HOMER, Trim Galore!, Bismark, Cell Ranger) plus an renv.lock for the R side (SVA, limma, DESeq2, Mfuzz, DiffBind, topGO, Seurat).

gaps.where: C1 (Guppy), C22 (AGAT), C23 (MMseqs2, IQ-TREE), C24 (ETE3), C29 (BLASTN, MITOS 2), C30 (CGView), C31 (Clustal Omega), C40 (IDR)
gaps.missing: These tools are named with NO version at all. Guppy is cited only by product URL despite basecalling model choice being the single largest determinant of downstream assembly; MITOS 2, CGView and Clustal Omega are hosted web services with neither version nor access date; IDR, MMseqs2, IQ-TREE (inside OrthoFinder), ETE3 and AGAT carry no version. These steps cannot exceed NI.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a complete versions table naming every tool, library and web service with exact version, and for hosted services the access date and the underlying database release.

gaps.missing: Version is pinned but NO invocation parameters are given: BUSCO lineage dataset (odb release) is missing for both C7 and C20; YaHS has no restriction-enzyme or resolution settings; RepeatModeler/RepeatMasker have no engine or library options; STAR has no alignment parameters; Portcullis, Mikado, Miniprot, PASA and Trinotate/PANTHER have no configuration or cutoffs; Mfuzz for peak clustering (C42) has no cluster number or fuzzifier, although the same package for transcript clustering (C35) does.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the full command lines (or the scripts) for each tool, including configuration files, database releases, and the BUSCO lineage datasets.

gaps.where: C6 (BlobTools taxonomy DB), C10 (RepBase), C11 (curated repeat library), C21 (Trinotate/PANTHER databases), C23/C27 (comparison proteomes and assemblies), C24 (reference species phylogeny), C28 (published chromosomal annotations), C19 (RepeatPeps.lib)
gaps.missing: Reference databases and comparison datasets are named but not versioned or deposited: no RepBase release, no BlobTools taxonomy dump date, no Swiss-Prot/Pfam/eggNOG releases behind Trinotate, no accessions or versions for the O. fusiformis proteome or for the U. unicinctus / P. maximus / L. longissimus assemblies used in macrosynteny, and the reference species tree used for gene family gain/loss is not deposited. The de novo curated repeat library produced in C10 - itself an input to C11, C19 and C39 - is likewise not deposited.
gaps.how_to_close: Give exact download URLs with release numbers and checksums for every reference database, deposit the curated repeat library and the reference species tree, and list the accession and assembly version of each comparison genome/proteome.

gaps.where: C13/C14/C15/C18 (RNA-seq evidence for annotation), C33-C35 (bulk transcriptomic profiling), C36-C43 (ATAC-seq), C44-C46 (EM-seq)
gaps.missing: The Data availability statement deposits only the newly generated whole-genome sequencing project (PRJEB101787). The bulk RNA-seq developmental time course, the ATAC-seq libraries and the EM-seq libraries that drive a large share of the results are referenced as 'all available RNA-seq datasets' or 'multi-omic datasets available for C. teleta' without accessions in this paper; the statement instead points to the Capitella Genome Project portal, whose URL is an unresolved placeholder (see liveness).
gaps.how_to_close: List the specific ENA/SRA/GEO accessions for every bulk RNA-seq, ATAC-seq and EM-seq library used, including the prior-publication datasets, rather than pointing to a portal.

gaps.missing: Eight steps depend on unpublished custom code or on irreducibly manual curation with no recorded decision trace: modified repeat-landscape script; gene-model filtering thresholds; gff-mining Python script; ETE3 gain/loss parsing; hypergeometric expansion test; ancestral linkage group assignment; methylation R scripts; and scRNA-seq cluster-resolution selection performed because a resolution 'seemed most biologically relevant' with subclusters merged by hand.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the custom scripts, and for the manual steps record the concrete outcome (chosen clustering resolution, subcluster merge map, gene-model filtering thresholds, linkage-group assignment table) as deposited supplementary files so the manual decision becomes replayable even if not re-derivable.

gaps.where: Data availability - Capitella Genome Project portal
gaps.missing: The portal that the paper designates as the access route for genome annotations, ATAC-seq and EM-seq data, BLAST and JBrowse is cited twice as the literal string '(weblink)'. There is no URL to resolve, so the primary declared access route for the derived resources of this paper is unresolvable at v1.
gaps.how_to_close: Replace the '(weblink)' placeholder with the real portal URL, and additionally deposit the annotation GFF, protein FASTA and processed ATAC/EM-seq tracks in an archival repository (Zenodo/ENA) so that access does not depend on a self-hosted service.

gaps.missing: Worm colony maintenance and larval collection/fixation, HMW gDNA extraction, ONT and Illumina sequencing, Proximo Hi-C library prep and sequencing, PCR + Sanger validation of mitochondrial gene order, riboprobe synthesis, whole-mount in situ hybridisation, and microscopy are physical steps, out of scope for computational reproduction; counted in W, not verdicted.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; the ENA-deposited project PRJEB101787 is the reproducible computational entry point for the assembly branch, and SRA PRJNA669754 for the scRNA-seq branch.
